findings.category: accessibility / inaccessible core interaction (Blood Smear Code, hem-01, no non-visual path)
findings.evidence: Independent judgement requested in (b). REPRODUCED: ariaSnapshot + CDP Accessibility.getFullAXTree of hem-01 contain only button 'Select a point on the scientific image' (img alt=''), the prompt 'Click the schistocyte (fragmented red cell).' and the context line; nothing lets a non-sighted user locate a schistocyte. GATING PROVEN via API on a fresh student who completed all 6 Microbiology/Biochemistry missions and unlocked both labs: POST /missions/hem-02/start -> 403 mission_locked 'Complete mission 01 to unlock.'; hem-03 -> 403; master-01 -> 403 lab_locked 'Clear 3 labs (2 of 3 cleared)'. So hem-01 blocks the whole Hematology lab and the Master Lab; there is no skip, alternative or teacher override. Completion without sight is only possible by blind guessing: keyboard-only scan of the Shift+Arrow grid from (0,0) (script r37B/hem01.mjs) needed 59 submissions = 58 wrong, score 0 of 180 XP, accuracy 2%; with an SR user at a realistic >=4 s per attempt that exceeds the 240 s mission limit (59 x 4 s = 236 s plus restarts), i.e. in practice not completable by skill nor reliably by chance. Rubric: 'P1 = inaccessible core interaction (a user of a core feature cannot complete the core flow)' matches literally (first mission of the first lab, and the gate to the Master Lab). Reasons I disagree with a P2 / 'documented limitation' classification as a SEVERITY: (1) severity is about impact, and the impact is a complete progression block for AT users; the documentation changes the handling, not the rating; (2) WCAG 1.1.1's test/exercise exception only excuses the text alternative of the image itself, it does not excuse that the learner cannot complete the exercise, and 2.1.1/1.3.1 say nothing against an alternative assessment, which is what is missing; (3) the existing P1 fix for bio-02 shows the team itself treated this class as P1. Reasons for leniency that I weighed: the task is intrinsically visual, the app does not claim accessibility, and engineering cannot invent an expert description. Therefore the CLOSURE is a product decision (see fix_hint), not a code bug, but it stays an open P1 until the owner decides.
findings.fix_hint: Needs an educator/owner decision, no engineering invention of expert content: (a) an educator-authored non-visual alternative assessment for hem-01 that satisfies the same competency (e.g. a described-features choice item: 'Which description matches a schistocyte?'), served instead of the point step when the learner opts in or the teacher enables it, with the same fragment/progression; or (b) an explicit teacher-granted accessibility exemption that marks hem-01 complete without score; or (c) the owner formally accepts the limitation and re-rates it P2 in the rubric. Independent of that, name the image on the control from step.data.image.caption ('Stylised blood smear (illustrative)') via aria-describedby.

findings.category: accessibility / forced-colors (Windows high contrast): selected state of a Select-result row is not perceivable
findings.evidence: REPRODUCED in Chromium with forcedColors: 'active' at 1280 (and 320/390/1440), section open, click 'Select Potassium result'. Computed styles: pressed button bg rgb(255,255,255) color rgb(0,0,0) border 1px rgba(5,0,73,0.8); unpressed bg rgb(255,255,255) color rgb(0,0,0) border 1px rgb(0,0,0). The only visible difference is a hairline dark-blue border instead of black; the screenshot shows the Potassium row looking identical to the other seven. The new rule .point-text button[aria-pressed=true]{background:#0f3031;...color:#fff} (refine.css:208) is overridden by forced colors and polish.css:325 adds no pressed style. The sibling engine keeps a visible state: a selected choice option has a 2px border vs 1px (same probe on Organ Rescue Mission: 2px vs 1px). The image marker ring is the only other cue and a keyboard-only forced-colors user working from the table would not see which row is armed before Submit (a wrong -10 XP submit is the cost).
findings.fix_hint: Inside @media (forced-colors: active) give .point-text button[aria-pressed="true"] a differentiating style that survives forced colors: border-width 3px or outline: 3px solid Highlight / background: Highlight; color: HighlightText (system colours), and optionally a leading check glyph or text 'Selected' in the button label.

findings.category: accessibility wording / consistency: raw flag code in the text version
findings.evidence: AX tree with the section open: row 'Potassium 6.4 mmol/L 3.5 - 5.1 H Select Potassium result'; cell name is the bare letter 'H' (a screen reader says 'H'). The same app prints flags through FLAG_WORDS (ui/common.tsx:88: L Low, H High, LL, HH) in the 'LABORATORY VALUES' block of other missions; PointTextAlternative prints row.flag raw (engines.tsx) while printing 'none' for the empty flag.
findings.fix_hint: Render FLAG_WORDS[row.flag] ?? row.flag (High) in PointTextAlternative (keep 'H' for sighted users with <abbr title='High'> if desired).

findings.category: layout / discoverability of the horizontal scroll region on phones
findings.evidence: At 320 and 360 px (scroll region 220-260 px wide, table min-width 440) with the section open and unscrolled, the visible columns are Test (sticky) and Result; Reference/Flag/Choose are cut mid-glyph ('R', '1', '3') with no scroll shadow, arrow or hint text, so the Select buttons are not visible until the learner discovers the sideways scroll; the table <caption> (which carries the disclaimer '(illustrative training image, not a real report)') lives inside the scrolling region, so on the first view it is cut after 'specimen indices'. Nothing overflows the page (documentElement overflow 0 at all widths) and 44 px targets hold; this is discoverability, not breakage.
findings.fix_hint: Add a one-line visible hint above the region on narrow screens ('Scroll sideways for the other columns'), or edge shadows (background-attachment: local gradients) on .point-text-scroll; move the <caption> outside the scrolling wrapper or let it wrap (caption-side/position: sticky; left: 0; max-width: 100vw).
